articles.title: Toddlers are not just little people. Their culture deserves respect | Arwa Mahdawi
articles.summary: Small children do not appreciate it when you join in with their singing or throw away their pee-covered leaves. And only a brute would suggest one of them might be tired. Nobody can be good at everything, can they? Take me, for example.
body: As it turns out, however, it may not just be the fact that I can’t hold a tune that’s upsetting her. I’m not saying that everything I know about parenting I learned from viral posts on the internet, but there was an illuminating tweet doing the rounds last week that said: “Today I learned if you try to sing along with a toddler when you have not been invited to do so, it is a sign of great disrespect in their culture.” I immediately went down an online rabbit hole and discovered various other people have made similar jokes. It’s a common issue.

articles.title: The Slightest Touch review – running marathons in Colin Farrell and Emma Fogarty’s odd-couple friendship
articles.summary: The pair, who met in 2010, are shown preparing for the Dublin race to raise awareness of Fogarty’s epidermolysis bullosa in Rachel Fleit’s considerate documentary. The personal scenes in this film from Rachel Fleit have been carefully controlled and curated, the privacy of both parties being…
body: Emma Fogarty is a smart, garrulous woman from Abbeyleix in County Laois in the Republic of Ireland who has EB: epidermolysis bullosa, a rare condition which means that her skin is permanently, agonisingly painful and requires a daily calvary of bandaging and re-bandaging. While getting an award at the People of the year event in 2010 for her campaigning work educating the public about this illness, Emma met and struck up a friendship with Colin Farrell, a supporter and patron of the EB charity Debra Ireland.

Their relationship continued for 15 years and in 2025 Farrell agreed to run the Dublin marathon for EB, with the final two miles pushing Emma in her modified wheelchair; a serious physical challenge for any runner. The film shows Emma and Colin in their different worlds preparing in their various ways for the marathon. (They are in fact only shown physically in the same space in the film’s final section.) But the film also shows a candidly emotional Farrell talking about his father, Eamon, who was on his deathbed in Ireland at the time, and talking also about his eldest son James, who was born with Angelman syndrome, similar to cerebral palsy.

articles.title: Sali Hughes on beauty: lactonic scents will have you smelling like cream soda – in a good way
articles.summary: These fragrances are on trend right now, and smelling creamy can, it turns out, be surprisingly pleasant. When the fragrance world picks a theme, it goes in hard. In the space of one month, I had close to a dozen new “lactonic” (that is, milky or creamy themed) perfumes to try.
body: Phlur, so beloved by gen Z, has leapt onboard the trend with Heavy Cream (from £26), available in fragrance and scented body spray. This is creamy, obviously, but also very sweet and immediately brings to mind Swizzels Drumstick lollies and the retro fizzy drink American cream soda. If this sounds like a kids’ party from hell, blame me, because it’s actually perfectly pleasant, got me heaps of compliments and got better and mellower as the hours passed. If you’re a milk with three sugars sort of a person, I think you may love it.

The Nue Co’s lactonic scent is called First Milk (£38 for 10ml), and is decidedly non-dairy in scent. This is almondine, a little peppery and unlike the others, has a translucence and a delicateness to the vanilla. It’s intimate, wholesome and comforting – a bit fluffy towel around a clean baby – but a little synthetic smelling. I get a nostalgic whiff of Silly Putty, and I say that with love.
points: These fragrances are on trend right now, and smelling creamy can, it turns out, be surprisingly pleasant.

articles.title: Egg Noodles Al Limone, Limone, Limone, Limone
articles.summary: One pot, four hits of lemon: Juice (limone #1) and zest (limone #2) in the cooking water, then more juice (limone #3) and zest (limone #4) to ﬁnish.
body: Want some protein here? Add one pound of peeled and deveined medium shrimp to the pot as soon as the pasta turns uncomfortably al dente.

Remove the zest from 2 lemons with a vegetable peeler in long, lengthwise strips. Chop the strips very fine. (You should have a heaping 2 Tbsp.) Transfer half the chopped zest to a large pot or Dutch oven. Reserve the remaining half.

Squeeze enough juice from the lemons to measure ½ cup (120 ml); reserve the remaining lemon for squeezing at the finish. Transfer ¼ cup (60 ml) of the juice to the pot with the zest and reserve the remaining juice for serving. Add 3½ cups (840 ml) water, 1 large shallot, peeled and thinly sliced, 2 Tbsp. (30 g) unsalted butter, 4 thyme sprigs, leaves stripped and stems discarded, and 1 Tbsp. Diamond Crystal kosher salt.

Serve topped with a big dollop of crème fraîche and a squeeze of lemon juice. Shower with the remaining 1 cup (2 oz./60 g) finely grated Parmigiano-Reggiano and pinches of flaky sea salt. (Yes, this is a lot of Parm! But stay with me here… it’s a vital balance to the punches of lemon.) Top with more thyme leaves, and if desired, cracked black pepper and chopped roasted hazelnuts.

articles.title: The 17 Best Airbnbs in Copenhagen Embrace Hygge
articles.summary: Book one of the best Airbnbs in Copenhagen ahead of your trip to the Danish capital—and get ready for tons of Scandinavian design inspiration.
body: If you’ve spent years saving photos of Copenhagen street style and Danish living rooms, the best way to really experience Scandi fashion and design is to go straight to the source—moodboards can only take you so far. Watch locals pedal past in color-blocked coats and billowy blouses, browse the racks at Hay House, and keep tabs on how many cafés have a Louis Poulsen pendant over their counter. Winter may be cold, but it’s a great time to go and see the city in action. Tivoli Gardens lights up for Christmas and the city settles into the candlelit coziness of hygge season.

A Copenhagen apartment delivers Scandinavian style up close. Think herringbone floors, tall windows, blonde wood, and a kitchen that’s set up to actually cook in. From canal-side flats in Christianshavn to a family house a short bike ride from the center, these are the Copenhagen Airbnbs at the top of our list.

articles.title: Mascara Has Entered Its Sophisticated Era
articles.summary: Modern mascara formulas make clumps, flakes, and raccoon eyes a thing of the past. Here’s what’s new, according to makeup artists and beauty experts.
body: Of all the products in our makeup bags, mascara might be the one to which we’re most loyal. Most of us found a formula we liked years ago, kept buying it, and never looked back. In the interim, foundations went matte and then glowy, skincare got upgraded with peptides and NAD+, and lipstick shade ranges have grown exponentially. Mascara on the other hand has worked pretty much the same: a fluffy blush dipped in rich black pigment.

That is, until now. The humble mascara is undergoing something of a renaissance. Tubing technologies promise effortless removal; long-wear formulas rival their longwear counterparts in the smudge department; rich browns and burgundies offer colorful alternative to the expected onyx; and meticulously engineered wands deliver the sort of precision even a makeup minimalist would love.

The reality is that mascara just works better now. The new formulas don’t flake by the afternoon or smudge into dark circles, and you can take them off without losing a bunch of lashes in the process. “I want my lashes to look beautiful at 9 a.m. and still look intentional at 9 p.m.,” says celebrity makeup artist Nam Vo. “I don’t need to check my under-eyes every 20 minutes.”

articles.title: On a Ranch in Wyoming, a Stressed-Out Editor Gets in Sync With a Lazy Horse
articles.summary: Traveler editor Hannah Towey attends a riding and writing retreat at Paintrock Canyon Ranch, where cell service is exchanged for creek cold plunges and cowgirl naps.
body: I used to avoid horses the same way I’d avoid palm readers. While my friends chased $5 readings in Downtown Manhattan, I preferred to keep the velvet curtain closed.

I was convinced that once a fortune teller held my hands in hers, she would trace a life line abruptly cut short or reveal a heart line splintered beyond repair. So I’d sit on the stoop, hands safely secured in the pockets of my jacket. Horses and psychics, I believed, shared the same dark, all-knowing eyes.
The 80,000-acre ranch is nestled between Wyoming's Bighorn Mountains and Paintrock Canyon.

The first time I rode a horse was 10 years ago in Costa Rica, my body clenched for the entirety of the 20-minute sunset beach stroll. “They can sense your fear,” I remember the guide telling me. “Just try to relax.”
